definitions: Relating to the Goths or their language.
Denoting a style of architecture prevalent in Western Europe from the 12th to the 16th centuries, characterized by pointed arches, rib vaults, and flying buttresses.
Relating to a literary genre popular in the 18th and early 19th centuries, characterized by an atmosphere of mystery and horror and a picturesque medieval setting.
Relating to a subculture characterized by dark attire, often black, and an interest in gothic music, art, and literature.
examples: Gothic art often depicted religious scenes.
The cathedral is a prime example of Gothic architecture.
He was dressed in typical Gothic fashion.
